title: Object name wrapped in quotes
description:
Code-style rule — an object name starts and ends with a literal double quote, almost always because a name was pasted straight out of a calculation. The quotes become part of the name, so every name-based access has to reproduce them.

Based on the fmCheckMate check "Quoted Object Name" — https://github.com/mrwatson-de/fmCheckMate-XSLT
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: The quotes are invisible as a mistake and visible as part of the name. Anything that looks the name up — a script calling it, a query filtering on it, a developer typing it again — has to include them.
rule.remediation: Rename the object without the surrounding quotes and update the references that relied on the quoted spelling.
